title: Saying You Don't Understand
goal: Explain what you missed and ask for repetition, slower speech or a clearer explanation.

runs.text: You do not have to pretend you understand. A useful repair tells the other person what help you need.

rows.text: You did not hear the words
You heard a word but do not know its meaning
You heard the sentence but the meaning is unclear
I'm not sure what you mean.
The speech is too fast for you
Could you say that more slowly?
You need the steps explained again
Could you walk me through it again?
Did you say Tuesday or Thursday?

runs.text: here means hear or understand what was said.

runs.text: means you now understand. Say it after the explanation actually helps. If it does not, try
I'm still not sure. Could you show me?
can ask someone to repeat. A short expression can also communicate surprise or challenge, depending on the encounter and delivery. A specific question often makes your intention clearer.
Ren's surprise and need to check are both visible. You can instead choose
when that expresses your intention better. Do not assume one short word is rude in every context.
Could you give me an example?
Do you mean the blue folder?
The following instructions belong to fictional scenes. Read both roles aloud on your own. Start with the support table; then hide it and try a different problem.
Meet me at the front desk at six
. You missed the time. Ask only about that detail. They repeat
The last day to send it
Someone gives three instructions too quickly:
Open the page, choose a time, and send the form
. Ask for slower speech. Rehearse their slower repetition, then confirm the three actions.
. You have a blue folder and a red one. Ask whether they mean the blue folder. They answer
Hide the model. Pick one of the situations and repair it without saying only
. Make your request specific enough to help the other person help you.
Sorry, what time did you say? — Six o'clock. — Okay, at six.
What does “deadline” mean? — The last day to send it. — Okay, I need to send it by Friday.
Could you say that more slowly? — Open the page. Choose a time. Send the form. — Got it: open, choose, and send.
Do you mean the blue folder? — No, the red one. — Oh, the red one. Okay.
Did you distinguish hearing from meaning? Did your request produce useful help? Could you confirm the corrected detail rather than repeat the original misunderstanding?
